thread.title: Booking Holdings: Great Business Despite Increasing Competition - Booking Holdings Inc. (NASDAQ:BKNG)

author: Ryan Teo
title: Booking Holdings: Great Business Despite Increasing Competition - Booking Holdings Inc. (NASDAQ:BKNG)
text:
Booking Holdings (NASDAQ: BKNG ), the new name for what was previously the Priceline Group, is the world's leader for booking online accommodation reservations and runs Booking.com, Priceline.com, Agoda.com, Kayak, OpenTable and Rentalcars.com.
BKNG data by YCharts
Booking is the leader in international markets. The industry has gone through a consolidation trend phase over the past years. The top leaders are gaining size through acquisitions, which keeps competition limited; Expedia (NASDAQ: EXPE ) added Travelocity and HomeAway to its portfolio, while Booking has added Kayak and OpenTable. Booking CEO Glenn Fogel has mentioned the company also wants to be a leader in alternative accommodation, and it seems that Booking and Airbnb ( AIRB ) are fighting an extremely close race .
(Source: Booking Holdings 10-K 2018 )
It's worth noting that the first quarter of the year tends to be the weakest profitability-wise . However, for the European and North American businesses, the highest levels of profitability are in the 2Q and 3Q of the year, which is when the highest levels of accommodation check-outs are experienced for the year. On the other hand, for the Asia-Pacific businesses, the highest levels of accommodation bookings are in the 3Q and 4Q of the year, with the highest levels of travel consumption seen in the 4Q. So, it is important to note the seasonality in the business.
Potential threats ahead Rising competition is an important risk factor in this sector. Booking Holdings and Expedia are the two leading players among online travel agencies. Globally, Booking’s highly profitable business is up against the rising threat of alternative accommodation, in particular Airbnb. In fact, Airbnb has been actively looking to add boutique hotels and bed and breakfasts to its platform.
In addition, Booking has recognised that Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL ), Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN ), Alibaba (NYSE: BABA ), Facebook (NASDAQ: FB ), Google (NASDAQ: GOOG ) and Tencent ( OTCPK:TCEHY ) are as big threats due to their more diversified resources.
For example, Google's travel meta-search services, Google Hotel Ads and Google Flights have achieved significant market share in a relatively short time. Meta-search services leverage their search technology to aggregate travel search results, effectively leveraging a new booking channel with extensive distribution. This is effectively competing for customers with Booking.
Also, Apple has a patent for iTravel , a mobile app that will allow the traveler to check in for a travel reservation. Passbook is essentially part of what the iTravel patent covers. It won't be a surprise to see Apple expanding or integrating its use into its ecosystem.
China Battleground In China, Booking is up against Ctrip (NASDAQ: CTRP ), China largest online travel agency in which it holds a 13% stake . It seems that Booking favors the strategy of partnering with domestic travel firms rather than directly entering the Chinese market. However, it is well-positioned to be competing in China with the help of partnerships, with Meituan-Dianping ( MEIT ) partnering with Agoda, while Booking is partnering with Ctrip.
Considering that Tencent and Alibaba both have their own online travel agencies, and domestic companies are taking sides in the battle between Alibaba and Tencent, it will be wise for Booking Holdings to hedge its bets through partnerships rather than directly competing in the tough China market.
The latest move in China is a global strategic partnership between Booking’s Agoda and Chinese Airbnb competitor Xiaozhu , to help the Chinese company expand its user base outside of the country. In the initial stages, both parties will share inventories with one another, which will mean an additional 100,000 listings on both platforms. It is pretty obvious that the partnership with Xiaozhu is a hedge against Ctrip and Airbnb and a bid to increase its global market share ahead of rival Expedia.
The Business Numbers Booking Holdings has a remarkable track record in creating value for shareholders over the years. Its business model of matching customers with industry operators and earning commission on every transaction means the company does not need to worry about inventory, cost and maintenance of property. This makes the business model exceptionally profitable.
The current gross profit margin stands at an extremely high 98%. In the past 8 years, it has undergone a tremendous gross margin expansion and has almost doubled its margins. High gross profit margins are the one of the most important factor of long-run performance. It is much more resilient and harder compared to operating profit margins. Comparing gross margins and operating margins, Booking's margins stand above those of Expedia and Ctrip.
BKNG Gross Profit Margin (TTM) data by YCharts BKNG Operating Margin (TTM) data by YCharts
Another key indicator is free cash flow. Cash flow is the oxygen of any business. The ability of a company to generate free cash flow gives the company a chance to add more value to shareholders. Ultimately, cash flow helps to determine long-term value to shareholders. Current EV/FCF is around 22.7, which makes EV/FCF/G seem around fair value range. Based on the EV/EBIT and EV/FCF ratios, it seems Booking is pretty fairly valued and worth an add if you already have some position in your portfolio.

Looking ahead However, we believe that tomorrow’s traveler should be able to book an entire vacation through voice activation, or skip the check-in line at a hotel or the key exchange for an apartment and unlock the door using one’s mobile phone. Tomorrow’s traveler shouldn’t have to spend days or weeks planning what to do on their trip, or wait on hold to speak with customer service when an artificial-intelligence driven messaging bot will be so much easier... We are in very early days, but that’s why KAYAK and OpenTable introduced voice search integrations with Amazon’s Alexa this year. It’s why Booking.com built a proprietary machine learning system in-house which is now powering its chat bot interface, which is already today able to respond to 50% of customer enquiries automatically."
- Glenn Fogel, CEO, in Letter to Shareholders 2018
Booking Holdings is a good company. It's expected the Asia-Pacific region will be the growth engine for the travel industry and can continue to expect a healthy growth rate for the years ahead. While Booking's network effect still remains intact, the company is still investing in businesses and AI to improve the global travel ecosystem. I expect its network effect to hold the advantage over other players. Its soft second-quarter guidance may have pushed the share price down, but the company is known for giving conservative guidance. More importantly, I believe that its high gross margins and free cash flow growth will ultimately help sustain long-term value for shareholders.
Disclosure: I/we have no positions in any stocks mentioned, but may initiate a long position in BKNG over the next 72 hours.
